_about: Inputs for the step B hand calcs (PLAN s17): brake heat (S-16), weld toes and rod-end threads (S-07b), steering free play (R-06). Keys ending _assumed are engineering assumptions; each limit cites its source, and a source only read second-hand says so.

brake_heat.endurance_km_basis: FSAE endurance: a single heat of about 22 km (rules D.12); confirm against the 2026 rules
brake_heat.front_share_from: LC3 (1.5 g braking): 2 x front Fx / (m g 1.5), the fixed-bias share at the limit
brake_heat.disc_material: 410 stainless (assumed; the disc is a quote line, H3)
brake_heat.disc_props_basis: density and specific heat from 410 stainless datasheets (AK Steel 7.74 g/cm3, about 460 J/kg K at 0-100 C) as relayed by a search, not opened; conductivity a typical value
brake_heat.disc_h_basis: No verified convection correlation for a small solid disc was found (Limpert and SAE 2006-01-1974 not accessible), so the disc temperature is given over a range of h; disc_h_design is used for the mount requirement
brake_heat.hat_basis: The CAD's hat (fsae_parts.disc, v1.7): a steel tube 56-60 mm radius from the disc's outboard face to the hub flange, 5.5 mm
brake_heat.hub_basis: The hub flange's inboard face and rim (60 mm radius, 14 mm wide; the outboard face is under the wheel) shed heat as they spin; h assumed. The hub and the upright are taken at one temperature (the bearings between them conduct well), so the budget counts both
brake_heat.contact_basis: Steel or titanium on steel at light clamp: of order 1e3-1e4 W/m2 K (assumed range). The mount is judged at the high end, where contacts resist least

float.basis: Floating disc on 6 bobbins: heat crosses two contacts (8 mm faces, relieved shoulders) and 6 mm of bobbin between them (a 12 mm bobbin). Ti-6Al-4V conducts about 6.7 W/m K against stainless 16 (typical handbook values); the design takes titanium

limits.loctite_641_basis: Henkel product page: service range -55 to +150 C (relayed by a search; the TDS hot-strength chart was not read)
limits.al7075_basis: Assumed. No primary exposure table was found (MMPDS not accessible); T73 is made by ageing at about 163 C (MIL-H-6088, second-hand), so strength loss from exposure should start above that. Confirm before publishing
limits.nylon_insert_nut_basis: FSAE T.8.2.3: nylon lock nuts only where the temperature does not exceed 80 C (read from a team's copy of the T.8 rules; confirm against the 2026 rules)

welds.basis: IIW recommendations (Hobbacher), load-carrying fillet weld: toe FAT 63, root FAT 36 on the throat, slope 3, read from secondary papers (Raftar et al., LUT; another quotes FAT 80 for the toe: the lower is used). The S-N line is taken on below the 1e7 knee with no endurance limit (conservative for variable amplitude). Confirm against the IIW 2016 tables
welds.throat_basis: Design rule for the drawings: every member-end fillet weld has a throat at least the tube wall (leg 1.4 x wall), so the throat stress equals the tube's

threads.engagement_basis: Rod-end shank in the tube insert: 1.5 x d (the engagement named in the BS EN 2791/2792 aerospace rod-end titles; text not read). Goes on the drawings with the jam nut
threads.strip_basis: Stripping area = 0.5 x pi x d x engagement: half the cylinder at the major diameter shears (the same rule as the Heli-Coil pull-out in HC-7), at 0.577 x the insert's yield
threads.fat_basis: EN 1993-1-9 Table 8.1: bolts and rods with rolled or cut threads in tension, detail category 50, slope 3 (confirmed second-hand: Fraunhofer, 2023). No credit taken for the jam nut's preload

free_play.rack_basis: Kaz rack: 'adjustable rack preload and lash' (kaztechnologies.com/steering-rack, read 2026-11-04); no figure published. 0.10 mm at the rack after adjustment is assumed
free_play.rod_end_basis: PTFE-lined rod ends run with near-zero radial play; 0.025 mm each is assumed (no Aurora figure read)
free_play.column_basis: Steering column, two universal joints and the wheel's quick release are chassis-side, not designed here; 2 deg is the share of the 7 deg budget they are allowed
free_play.c_factor_from: vehicle.json steering.rack_c_factor_mm_per_rev_assumed (75 mm/rev; the Kaz rack's own 4.71 in/rev, 119.6 mm, gives less play at the wheel)

arb_bar_fatigue.basis: Marin surface factor ka = a Sut^b (Shigley Table 6-2). The bar's body and its R4 shoulder fillets are specified form-ground (usual for torsion bars); the spline is cut, so machined. Read second-hand
arb_bar_fatigue.reliability_basis: 99 % reliability (Shigley Table 6-5), the same factor the upright's fatigue uses (upright_fea.py, upright_fatigue.py). Left out until the step E audit, which is what failed the 150 ksi bar
